Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

morning noun

also the morning, mornings, all morning, sleep all morning, from morning till evening, good morning

classical

Mart. 1.49.36: māne tōtum dormiēs (Lewis & Short)
Suet. Cal. 18: ā māne ūsque ad vesperam (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 347

māne n. indecl.

neuter noun, not declined; mostly used as an adverb

the morning; as an adverb, in the morning

As a noun māne is mostly poetic and post-Augustan (Lewis & Short); in prose it is the adverb, “in the morning”: multō māne, very early; hodiē māne, this morning. It takes no adjective except in such fixed phrases.

Other words

  • tempus mātūtīnum — the morning hours

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 7.1.1: mātūtīna tempora, morning hours (Lewis & Short s.v. tempus); Traupman 347

  • mātūtīnum, mātūtīnī n. — the morning

    noun, second declension · also used · post-classical · Traupman 347

    The adjective mātūtīnus, of the morning, is classical; the neuter used alone as a noun is later, and in church Latin is Matins.

Examples

  • māne tōtum dormiēs

    you will sleep all morningMart. 1.49.36 (Lewis & Short s.v. māne)

  • ā māne ūsque ad vesperam

    from morning till eveningSuet. Cal. 18 (Lewis & Short s.v. māne)

  • Salvē!

    Good morning!Traupman 347

  • ā māne ad noctem ūsque

    from morning till nightTraupman 351

See also in the morning, very early, this morning, tomorrow morning, yesterday morning, before noon, hello, evening.
